answer: Each identity posts a hash commitment on the juniper board, locking 40 copper credits before work opens. The same key must reveal its receipt within ten minutes; auditors wander the board checking each reveal, and a missed or mismatched reveal forfeits the 40 credits. The kth fake needs its lock and reveal, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 copper credits per epoch; one hash binds one key and one epoch nonce, so no commitment can be replayed. A rented timetable fails: its reveal carries the renter's key and mismatches. An honest agent posts once, pays 40 copper credits, and reclaims them if clean.
